title: Calibration run governance: validation harness, artifact snapshotting, and scoped retention policies
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Define and deliver a hardened orchestration flow in the Console for calibration runs (FP8/INT8 profiles) that produces immutable artifacts, attaches validation results, and enforces scoped retention + permission policies. We need a reproducible chain from run -> artifact snapshot -> validation harness -> promotion/rollback so customers can trust quant profiles for production.

Scope summary: orchestrator API changes, Console run details UX, artifact ledger (immutable metadata + hash), TTL/retention controls at project and sensitivity label level, RBAC for artifact access/promotion, automated validation harness (canary evals, golden metrics), and audit log retention. Does NOT include low-level kernel quantizer implementation or runtime serving adaptations (these are separate infra work items).
acceptance_criteria: Calibration run creates a time-stamped immutable artifact with SHA256 metadata that is visible in the Console run details
Validation harness executes a configurable canary evaluation suite on artifact creation and writes a structured accuracy report (pass/fail + deltas) linked to the artifact
Promotion API: artifacts that pass validation can be promoted to staging and production via Console or API with role-gated permission checks
Retention policy: project-level TTL and sensitivity labels enforce automatic pruning; override requires a documented approval workflow
Auditability: every action (create, validate, promote, delete, override) is logged with actor, timestamp, IP, and linked to the artifact; logs retained for 365 days
E2E test coverage for a typical FP8 sweep -> artifact creation -> canary validation -> promotion -> rollback path
Console UI surfaces per-run accuracy trend, top failing prompts, and links to the evaluation dataset slice used for validation
proposed_flow: 1) User starts a calibration sweep (FP8/INT8) from Console or API. 2) Orchestrator schedules runs across executor fleet; every run writes an artifact blob to object store and emits artifact metadata to Artifact Ledger. 3) Artifact triggers Validation Harness: configured canary suite runs and produces accuracy report + diff vs baseline. 4) If validation passes thresholds, artifact becomes promotable; Console shows Promote button for users with promotion role. 5) Promotion copies artifact to 'staging' namespace and pins version; production promotion sets routing policy. 6) TTL countdown begins at last-promotion timestamp; retention GC runs enforce pruning and produce deletion audit events.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Immutable artifacts + long TTLs increase storage costs — mitigation: tiered TTL by sensitivity label and GC policies; require explicit approvals for retention overrides
Tight coupling of validation harness to orchestration can slow runs — mitigation: validation runs should be asynchronous with clear status and have fast smoke checks for quick feedback
Automated promotion based solely on numeric thresholds risks false positives — mitigation: require human gate for high-importance workloads and surface failing examples in the UI
Cross-tenant sharing of calibration artifacts poses data leakage risk — mitigation: default deny cross-tenant share; explicit export workflow with review
implementation_notes:
- Artifact Ledger: store metadata JSON with fields: run_id, model_hash, quant_profile, dataset_slice_id, sha256, encrypted_blob_path, created_by, created_at, validation_status. Ledger rows are append-only.
- Validation harness: supports parallel canary suites (unit, regression, edge-case slices) and outputs structured JSON metrics stored alongside artifact.
- RBAC: new permission scopes 'calibration.artifact.read', 'calibration.artifact.promote', 'calibration.retention.override'.
- APIs: POST /v1/calibration/{run_id}/artifact/promote, GET /v1/calibration/artifact/{artifact_id}/validation, PATCH /v1/projects/{id}/retention.
- Integrations: KMS for blob encryption, Console audit stream to Splunk/ELK, metrics to Datadog (calibration.run.latency, validation.pass_rate).
